chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Believer cannot marry a Hostile woman (Nasibi), the one who is well known with that.

key_terms.النَّاصِبَة: A female descendant or follower of the Nasiba, known for enmity towards Ali (AS) and the Ahl al-Bayt.
key_terms.بِذَلِكَ: With that, referring to the characteristic of being Nasibi.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a Nasibi woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a specific legal criterion for marital compatibility, prohibiting marriage to a 'Nasibi' woman known for her enmity toward the Ahl al-Bayt. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'Wilayah' (loyalty to the Imams) as a foundational virtue in family structure, ensuring that the domestic sphere aligns with theological identity. The term 'known for' (al-ma'rufa) indicates that this is not merely a theoretical label but a practical assessment of her public reputation and adherence to anti-Ahl al-Bayt sentiments.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Salih, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Believer cannot marry a Hostile woman (Nasibi), the one (who is) well known with that’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A believer must not marry one who is hostile to ‘A’immah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, and his hostility is well known.’”
